stem.en: In the straight-water world, salt does not dissolve. Kabir says "so salt would be useless". What does the failure to dissolve actually tell you?

text.en: Dissolving salt needs water's charged corners to pull each ion away from the lattice. Straight water has no charged corners, so the lattice holds.

feedback.en: Hardness is not the issue; the same salt dissolves in bent water and it is the same crystal. What changed is what the water can grab.
The sim holds the glass at room temperature. It is a liquid there only because the sim forces it; the salt still will not dissolve, because the water has no partial charges.

text.en: Salt would dissolve in oil instead.

feedback.en: Oil has no charged corners either. Salt in oil does exactly what salt in straight water does: nothing.

explanation.en: Dissolving is a pull. The puller is the partial charge on the water molecule. Remove the bend, remove the charge, remove the pull.
